description: Figure 5(a) displays the training loss curves for different methods as a function of training steps, plotted on a linear scale from 0 to 143,000 steps on the x-axis and loss values from approximately 94 to 100 on the y-axis. The plot includes five lines, each representing a different model configuration: Vanilla (purple line with circle markers), StrmLLM(n=64) (orange line with square markers), SepLLM(n=64) (blue line with diamond markers), SepLLM(n=128) (green line with triangle markers), and SepLLM(n=64,H) (red line with cross markers). All methods start at a loss value near 100 at step 0. The Vanilla model shows a steady decline in loss, reaching approximately 96.5 by step 143,000. StrmLLM(n=64) begins with a steeper drop, reaching a loss of about 95.5 by step 50,000, then plateaus slightly before continuing to decline to approximately 95.8. SepLLM(n=64) follows a similar trajectory to StrmLLM(n=64), ending slightly higher at around 96.0. SepLLM(n=128) exhibits a faster initial drop than the n=64 variants, reaching approximately 95.2 by step 50,000, and continues to decrease to about 95.5. The SepLLM(n=64,H) variant starts with a sharp decline, reaching a loss of about 95.0 by step 50,000, and ends at approximately 95.3, showing the lowest final loss among all methods.
